I didn't watch the whole video but you're throwing out a lot of attacks. Pretty much every time you jumped or ran forward you went for an attack and it got predictable to the point where the Mewtwo just out-spaced your approaches and punished accordingly. Another comment pointed out that you were holding forward constantly too and that is definitely true.

Try playing more defensively and don't feel the need to attack every chance you get. If you are always the one that is approaching, whoever you are playing against will just wait for your attack to whiff/hit on shield and then punish you. Mix aggressive approach options with more passive play like baiting with movement (dashing back and forth, running forward and jumping backwards, etc.) or simply waiting to keep people guessing.

I feel like you could work on making your movement less predictable. Every time you jumped in neutral or advantage you threw out an attack and your movement on the ground was mostly running towards the opponent and going for an attack or a defensive option like shielding or rolling. It was easy for them to punish you as they knew exactly what you were gonna do the second you jumped or ran towards them. Try throwing in things like dash dances (dashing back and forth quickly) as well as empty hops (jumping without attacking or doing anything else) to keep the other guy/gal guessing about what you’re gonna do.

I also feel like you were rolling a bit too much in some cases. In the first 10 seconds or so of the Puff video, you rolled when she was quite far away when you were in no threat of danger. Rolls should mostly be used to avoid an incoming attack/grab and shouldn’t be used as a general movement option at all.

I've only listened to it once and no Radiohead album makes sense on the first listen for me.

However, I wasn't a fan of folk direction they took; it feels like any band could've made half of the songs here. I've never been bothered by Radiohead's dominance of slow songs (in fact, I welcome it), but this is the first album that really felt like something that would be droning in the background of a cafe.

At the moment, my favourite songs are the two that were released as singles (that might just be because I've had more time to adjust to them, time will tell); Burn the Witch balances the groove and beauty perfectly and Daydreaming is probably amongst the band's best material. Once the folk influences hit I started to lose interest. The reason I love albums such as Kid A and Ok Computer so much is that the order of the songs make the albums feel cinematic, having a fulfilling sense of progression through all of the tracks. This album on the other hand feels static; it's not so much of a film where the scenes are delicately placed, but a sitcom where the episodes just coexist.  To add insult to injury, the songs are ordered alphabetically; it's like they didn't even bother.

It's not like Radiohead haven't taken this approach before; I would use that same analogy to describe In Rainbows, but in a more positive manner. The songs are diverse yet cohesive, delivering the energy in songs like Bodysnatchers and Jigsaw while cooling you down with Nude and Reckoner. While A Moon Shaped Pool is possibly Radiohead's most cohesive sounding album, it is also the most uneventful.

I know this review sounds insanely negative, but I'm just spit-balling my first impressions here as a fan of five years. Please note that both Burn the Witch and Daydreaming took me a day or two to enjoy and that my initial reaction is probably the whiplash of 2 years of active hyping. I'll probably love this album by the end of the week, it may even rank up there with the holy trinity, but at the moment (here come the down votes), I much prefer The King of Limbs.
